heading: The mortgage protection letter in 71 seconds
name: That mortgage protection letter after closing: what it is
description: Why a mortgage protection letter can arrive after closing, why it may not be from your lender, and 5 things to check before you reply. Mortgage protection is life insurance, and buying it is your choice.
transcript: That mortgage protection letter after closing: here is what it is, and what to check before you reply. A home purchase creates public records. Deeds and mortgages are recorded in local land records. Those records are generally open to the public. A letter that shows your lender's name did not necessarily come from your lender. It may be an advertisement for life insurance. Mortgage protection is life insurance, and buying it is your choice. PMI is different. A lender may require it, and it protects the lender. Before you reply, check 5 things. 1. Find the names of the agent and the insurance company. 2. Confirm both are licensed with your state insurance department. 3. Ask if it is level term or decreasing term. 4. Count the life insurance you already have. 5. Get a second quote on level term, and compare. An advertisement does not need an answer. And a letter is not a reason to drop coverage you own. Want to talk it through? Schedule a time at honorbrook-insurance.com or call (301) 615-8289.
